subject: math
source: IB Diploma Programme Mathematics: analysis and approaches guide (first assessment 2021), HL (SL core + additional higher level) — topics 1–5 and toolkit/exploration

weeks.topic: Scientific notation and counting principles (SL 1.1, AHL 1.10)
objectives: Operate with numbers in the form a × 10^k
Use the GDC efficiently for calculations and graphs
Round answers to an appropriate degree of accuracy
Count arrangements using permutations and combinations

weeks.topic: Arithmetic sequences and series (SL 1.2)
objectives: Use the nth term formula of an arithmetic sequence
Find sums of arithmetic series using sigma notation
Model real-life contexts with arithmetic sequences

weeks.topic: Geometric sequences and series; infinite geometric series (SL 1.3, 1.8)
objectives: Use nth term and sum formulas for geometric sequences
Decide when an infinite geometric series converges
Calculate the sum to infinity

weeks.topic: Financial applications: compound interest and depreciation (SL 1.4)
objectives: Calculate compound interest with different compounding periods
Model depreciation with geometric sequences
Use the GDC finance solver

weeks.topic: Laws of exponents and introduction to logarithms (SL 1.5, 1.7)
objectives: Apply the laws of exponents, including rational exponents
Understand logarithms as the inverse of exponentials
Evaluate logarithms in base 10 and base e

weeks.topic: Laws of logarithms and exponential equations (SL 1.7)
objectives: Apply the laws of logarithms
Use the change of base formula
Solve exponential equations using logarithms

weeks.topic: Proof: deductive, induction, contradiction and counterexample (SL 1.6, AHL 1.15)
objectives: Construct proofs working from LHS to RHS
Use correct mathematical notation and language
Prove statements by mathematical induction
Prove by contradiction and disprove by counterexample

weeks.topic: Binomial theorem with fractional and negative indices (SL 1.9, AHL 1.10)
objectives: Expand (a + b)^n for positive integer n
Use Pascal's triangle and nCr
Find a specific term or coefficient in an expansion
Extend the binomial theorem to rational n and state its validity

weeks.topic: Complex numbers: Cartesian form and the Argand diagram (AHL 1.12)
objectives: Perform arithmetic with complex numbers in Cartesian form
Represent complex numbers on an Argand diagram
Find complex roots of quadratic equations

weeks.topic: Complex numbers: modulus–argument and Euler forms (AHL 1.13)
objectives: Convert between Cartesian, polar and Euler forms
Multiply and divide complex numbers in polar form
Interpret operations geometrically

weeks.topic: De Moivre's theorem and roots of complex numbers (AHL 1.14)
objectives: Prove and apply De Moivre's theorem
Find nth roots of complex numbers
Use conjugate roots of polynomials with real coefficients

weeks.topic: Functions, composites and inverses; odd, even and self-inverse (SL 2.1–2.5, AHL 2.14)
objectives: Use function notation, domain, range and equations of lines
Form composite and inverse functions
Identify odd, even and self-inverse functions

weeks.topic: Quadratic and polynomial functions (SL 2.6, 2.7, AHL 2.12)
objectives: Use standard, factorised and vertex forms of a quadratic
Solve quadratic equations and inequalities
Apply the factor and remainder theorems
Use sums and products of roots of polynomials

weeks.topic: Rational, exponential and log functions; partial fractions (SL 2.8–2.10, AHL 2.13, 1.11)
objectives: Sketch rational functions with oblique and vertical asymptotes
Sketch exponential and logarithmic graphs
Decompose rational expressions into partial fractions

weeks.topic: Review: number, algebra, complex numbers and functions
objectives: Consolidate sequences, logarithms and binomial expansion
Practise function and graph questions
Identify personal gaps for the holiday
Consolidate complex numbers and proof by induction

weeks.topic: Transformations, modulus functions and inequalities (SL 2.11, AHL 2.15, 2.16)
objectives: Apply and combine graph transformations
Sketch y = |f(x)|, y = f(|x|) and y = 1/f(x)
Solve polynomial and modulus inequalities

weeks.topic: Statistics: sampling, data, summary measures and regression (SL 4.1–4.4, 4.10)
objectives: Choose sampling techniques and identify bias
Calculate summary statistics with the GDC
Use correlation and regression lines appropriately

weeks.topic: Probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem (SL 4.5, 4.6, 4.11, AHL 4.13)
objectives: Use sample spaces, Venn and tree diagrams
Calculate conditional probabilities
Test for independent and mutually exclusive events
Use Bayes' theorem for two or three events

weeks.topic: Discrete and continuous random variables; variance (SL 4.7, AHL 4.14)
objectives: Construct probability distributions for discrete random variables
Calculate expected value E(X)
Find variance and use E(aX + b), Var(aX + b)
Use probability density functions for continuous variables

weeks.topic: Binomial and normal distributions (SL 4.8, 4.9, 4.12)
objectives: Model with B(n, p) and calculate probabilities
Use the normal distribution and inverse normal
Standardise values to find unknown μ or σ

weeks.topic: 3D geometry and trigonometry of triangles (SL 3.1–3.3)
objectives: Solve problems with 3D solids, distances and angles
Use sine and cosine rules, including the ambiguous case
Apply trigonometry to bearings and elevation

weeks.topic: Radians, unit circle and identities incl. compound angles (SL 3.4–3.6, AHL 3.10)
objectives: Use radians, arc length and sector area
Apply Pythagorean and double angle identities
Use compound angle identities

weeks.topic: Circular, reciprocal and inverse trigonometric functions (SL 3.7, AHL 3.9, 3.11)
objectives: Sketch and transform circular functions
Define sec, cosec and cot and their identities
Use arcsin, arccos and arctan and symmetry properties

weeks.topic: Solving trigonometric equations (SL 3.8)
objectives: Solve trigonometric equations in a finite interval
Solve quadratic equations in sin x or cos x
Use identities and the GDC to find all solutions
Solve equations involving reciprocal and compound-angle identities

weeks.topic: Vectors: concepts, components and the scalar product (AHL 3.12, 3.13)
objectives: Represent vectors in 2D and 3D with components
Find magnitudes, unit vectors and position vectors
Use the scalar product to find angles

weeks.topic: Vector equations of lines and the vector product (AHL 3.14–3.16)
objectives: Write vector and parametric equations of lines
Classify lines as parallel, intersecting or skew
Use the vector product to find areas and normals

weeks.topic: Mid-year exams: algebra, functions, statistics and trigonometry
objectives: Complete timed papers with and without a calculator
Apply topics 1–4 including AHL content
Reflect on errors and time management

weeks.topic: Planes, systems of linear equations and intersections (AHL 3.17, 3.18, 1.16)
objectives: Write vector and Cartesian equations of planes
Find intersections and angles between lines and planes
Solve systems of up to three linear equations

weeks.topic: Limits, first principles, continuity and differentiability (SL 5.1, 5.2, AHL 5.12)
objectives: Understand the derivative as a limit and as rate of change
Interpret dy/dx and f'(x) notation
Differentiate from first principles
Discuss continuity and differentiability at a point

weeks.topic: Differentiation rules: power, chain, product and quotient (SL 5.3–5.6)
objectives: Differentiate polynomials, sin, cos, e^x and ln x
Apply chain, product and quotient rules
Find tangents and normals

weeks.topic: Further derivatives and implicit differentiation (AHL 5.14, 5.15)
objectives: Differentiate tan, sec, cosec, cot, a^x and log_a x
Differentiate inverse trigonometric functions
Use implicit differentiation

weeks.topic: Stationary points, optimisation and related rates (SL 5.7, 5.8, AHL 5.14)
objectives: Use the second derivative to classify stationary points
Find points of inflexion
Solve optimisation and related rates problems

weeks.topic: Introduction to integration: anti-derivatives and area (SL 5.5)
objectives: Integrate x^n as the reverse of differentiation
Find the constant of integration from boundary conditions
Use definite integrals to find area under a curve

weeks.topic: IA exploration: choosing a topic and writing a proposal
objectives: Explore personal interests with mathematical potential
Write a focused aim for the exploration
Understand criteria A–E for the exploration

weeks.topic: IA exploration: mathematical research and first outline
objectives: Identify the mathematics needed for the chosen aim
Collect or generate data where relevant
Plan the structure of the exploration

weeks.topic: End-of-year exams: DP1 mathematics HL
objectives: Sit Paper 1 and Paper 2 style school exams
Demonstrate all DP1 content under timed conditions
Show full working for method marks
Attempt longer problem-solving questions

weeks.topic: Review: DP1 reflection and exploration plan for the holidays
objectives: Analyse exam results by topic
Set a revision and exploration timeline
Prepare data or research for the IA over the break
